question.problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $P(0,1,1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-p)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
